previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with left flank pain, fever, and nausea, initially concerning for pyelonephritis. Imaging and urology evaluation showed no active kidney infection or obstruction, with stable bilateral hydronephrosis. Instead, he was found to have cellulitis of the right foot, likely from trauma and recent toenail removal. He developed an allergic reaction to linezolid, which was discontinued, and was successfully treated with clindamycin. His pain improved with management of muscle spasms and infection. Hypertension was managed with restart of amlodipine. He remained afebrile with stable labs, including creatinine around 3.4, and was discharged home in improved condition on a full course of clindamycin, with follow-up planned for blood pressure, mood, and vaccination status.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of foot, except toes
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the kidneys were
obtained.  Patient was unable to cooperate with the entire exam an was

COMPARISON:  CT performed on ___.

FINDINGS: 

Limited renal ultrasound was performed.

The right kidney measures 8.3 cm in length. There is mild right hydronephrosis
as seen on the previous CT. The renal cortex is thin, compatible with chronic
renal disease.

The patient was exquisitely tender along the left flank, limiting evaluation
of the left kidney and perinephric space.  The left kidney measures 9.8 cm in
length. There is severe left hydronephrosis, as seen on prior CT. The left
renal cortex is thinned, compatible with chronic renal disease. A nephrostomy
tube is partially seen coiled within the left renal collecting system. 
Limited ultrasound at the skin site of the nephrostomy tube demonstrates no
discrete abscess or fluid collection.

IMPRESSION: 

Limited renal ultrasound demonstrates severe left and mild right
hydronephrosis, as seen on prior imaging.  A left nephrostomy tube is
partially visualized without any evidence of subcutaneous abscess or
collection at the skin entry site.

If there is concern for deeper infection, a CT is recommended for further
evaluation.

Chronic posttraumatic changes of the left iliac bone, stable when compared to

related to orthopedic hardware.  There is a chronic compression deformity of
